SparkR / SPARKR-131
Have the ability to create and return a LabeledPoint RDD to be used with MLlib
Issue Type: New Feature
Assignee: Unassigned
Created: 28/Oct/14 11:58 AM
Labels: MLlib
Priority: Major
Reporter: Oscar Olmedo

Having a LabeledPoint is the first step to using MLlib

Perhaps the data is comma separated with the last column as the label 1 or 0
e.g.
3.4,6.0,7.1,3.5,7.3,1
4.3,2.2,3.3,9.0,4.5,1
4.4,6.7,5.5,7.8,2.3,0
...

readPartition=function(part)

{ part = strsplit(part, ",", fixed = T)[[1]] arr=c(part[length(part)],part[1:(length(part)-1)]) label=part[length(part)] vector=part[1:(length(part)-1)] return(list(label=label,vector=vector)) }

rdd <- textFile(sc,datafile)
points <- LabeledPoints(cache(lapply(rdd, readPartition)))

LabeledPoints() return a LabeledPoints RDD that can be passed to MLlib.

In order to use MLlib library the build.sbt must be modified by adding
"org.apache.spark" % "spark-mllib_2.10" % "1.1.0"
to the libraryDependencies

Re: Have the ability to create and return a LabeledPoint RDD to be used with MLlib

There is architectural issue on how to integrate the MLLIB into SparkR. In pySpark, py4j is used for bi-directional RPC between a jvm task and a python interpreter, so MLLIB can be called from Python. For SparkR, I can't find such a project that can serve such purpose. rJava allows R calls into Java in the same process, not inter-process. Maybe it is possible to use JRI to launch a in-process R engine within a jvm task, but not sure about the license issue (JRI is LGPL license) and not sure about the functional completeness of the R engine of JRI.

I was able to call MLlib with rJava by first writing a separate java function to convert the jrdd to a labeled point, then with R using rJava call the MLlib method and pass the converted jrdd that is of type JavaRDD<LabeledPoint>. I had to included MLlib into the SparkR jar build.

I don't think JRI would be needed since the java object would exist inside of R, then the java MLlib object would be called from within R, and not the other way around. I'm not familiar with py4j, but taking a quick look at it, and correct me if I'm wrong, it looks like it does the same things that rJava does. "Py4J enables Python programs running in a Python interpreter to dynamically access Java objects in a Java Virtual Machine"

I manage to use MLlib in SparkR by getting the underlying JavaRDD of a R RDD of type labeledpoint(numeric, numeric vector) (using SparkR:::getJRDD) then converting it to a Scala RDD of type LabeledPoint and passing it to the MLlib function using rJava:

SparkR's Naive Bayes example https://gist.github.com/kiendang/4d73612ce35cbf943b0f
Scala code to convert types https://gist.github.com/kiendang/4aef5fb0c249613dec65

But in order to do so, I have to use Rserve to use the R unserialize function in the step where I convert a Scala RDD of serialized R objects to a Scala RDD of Scala LabeledPoint. I understand that I may call the R interpreter instead of Rserve but I'm not sure how.

Currently my company is working on integration of SparkR and Spark's MLlib. I'm thinking of adding a new discussion to move this forward and would love to hear your opinions.

Re: Have the ability to create and return a LabeledPoint RDD to be used with MLlib

Kien Dang I will take a look at your code, it looks really nice. Perhaps Sun Rui had a good point in the earlier comment regarding py4j, which I think the R equivalent is Rengine. In my opinion there are two paradigms, either R is called from within the Java code, in which case the unserialization takes place there or, something like the python Pickler class and unserialization takes place before the conversion to labeledPoint. Maybe my earlier thinking of trying to avoid calling R within Java was wrong. Then again SparkR makes use of Rscript, so I wonder is there a difference between using Rscript and Rengine? Considering that instead of Java calling R explicitly with Rengine, SparkR is calling R implicitly with Rscript.

My idea was lapply would be called first to put the data into a label/vector format then the output could be converted to a labeledPoint format before being passed to the MLlib function.
